title: FAIRE-Seq/Sono-Seq
scope: Illumina explanatory schematic: leftmost grouped caption and yellow-highlighted accessible chromatin icon; Open DNA -> Crosslink protein and DNA with formalin -> Sonicate -> Phenol extract and purify DNA from the aqueous phase -> DNA. There are three visible transformation captions, three rightward arrows, no drawn branches and no sequencing/library block. The graph resolves this route as FAIRE at schematic level, adds only broad text-supported readout blocks and an abstract-supported Sono-Seq alternative, and explicitly marks the unresolved applicability of the extraction block to Sono-Seq. Related publications are catalogue background and are not used to supply additional operations. No historical-priority or equivalence claim is made.

operations.label: Crosslink protein and DNA with formalin
operations.description: Acts on chromatin containing exposed and nucleosome-associated DNA. Formaldehyde fixation produces crosslinked protein-DNA associations; relatively nucleosome-depleted DNA is less efficiently crosslinked. The source caption says formalin; the card and FAIRE paper identify formaldehyde. This is reagent addition acting on existing chromatin, not production of an independent nucleosome reagent.
operations.mechanism: Preferential crosslinking of nucleosome-associated DNA underlies later FAIRE partitioning; crosslinking is not claimed to be uniform or absolutely specific.
operations.information_effect: Fixation preserves protein-occupancy-dependent differences in crosslinkability on genomic DNA; it introduces no sequence barcode.

DNA in nucleosome depleted regions of chromatin (for example through the activity of a sequence-specific regulatory factor) is much less efficiently crosslinked to protein12.

operations.label: Sonicate
operations.description: Acts on fixed chromatin to shear it into fragments. The free black segment and faded nucleosome icons illustrate the accessible DNA component of a heterogeneous sheared sample; the input to FAIRE phenol extraction still includes crosslinked protein-DNA material. Lysis is stated in the card but is not a separate operation in this diagram.
operations.mechanism: Physical chromatin fragmentation by sonication; no cleavage enzyme or crosslink-reversal chemistry is drawn.
operations.information_effect: Fragment sequences retain genomic identity. Sono-Seq uses the distribution of breakage in conjunction with size selection as an accessibility-associated signal.

operations.label: Phenol extract and purify DNA from the aqueous phase
operations.description: Acts on sonicated crosslinked chromatin. For FAIRE, phenol-chloroform partitioning preferentially retains relatively protein-uncrosslinked DNA in the aqueous phase and excludes crosslinked protein-DNA complexes to the interphase. The retained aqueous fraction is purified to yield the depicted DNA endpoint. This broad extraction/purification block is not decomposed into unshown execution steps.
operations.mechanism: Differential phase partitioning selects DNA that is not covalently trapped with proteins, enriching rather than perfectly isolating nucleosome-depleted genomic regions.
operations.information_effect: The retained physical carrier is genomic DNA. Relative fragment abundance reflects the selection; protein identity and direct proof of regulatory activity are not retained as a dedicated measurement.

operations.label: Sono-Seq size selection and short-read sequencing (abstract-supported alternative; not drawn)
operations.description: In the Sono-Seq alternative, sonicated crosslinked chromatin is combined with size selection and massively parallel short-read sequencing to yield an accessibility-associated breakage profile. It is not appended downstream of FAIRE extraction.
operations.information_effect: The readout carrier is size-selected genomic DNA derived from sonicated chromatin. Genomic read locations report accessibility-associated breakage, especially at active promoters, rather than establishing perfect nucleosome absence.

method_scopes.rationale: The visible fixation -> sonication -> aqueous-phase phenol extraction/purification route is supported as FAIRE. Library preparation and sequencing are explicit text-supported extensions beyond the drawn DNA endpoint. FAIRE means Formaldehyde Assisted Isolation of Regulatory Elements; FAIRE-seq specifies sequencing detection rather than a distinct isolation chemistry. The leftmost yellow-highlighted chromatin icon is explanatory, not an extra step. The 2006 Hogan paper supports FAIRE isolation coupled to microarrays; it does not verify a sequencing library. Sequencing detection is supported here by the inspected 2009 and 2012 FAIRE protocol texts.

method_scopes.rationale: Sono-Seq is a distinct assay, expanded in the drawing as sonication of cross-linked chromatin. Its primary abstract directly supports crosslinked chromatin, sonication, size selection and short-read sequencing, with a breakage pattern distinct from FAIRE. The two routes represented here are method alternatives, not a depicted physical split. The supplied abstract does not establish whether the grouped phenol/aqueous-phase block applies to Sono-Seq or how it relates to crosslink reversal, so o_faire_extract is not assigned to this method.

corrections.diagram_observation: After Sonicate, the nucleosome icons are faded and detached from the prominent black DNA line; no intermediate mixture or retained crosslinked fraction is separately drawn.
corrections.primary_statement: The FAIRE source says chromatin is first crosslinked, then sheared and phenol-chloroform extracted; most genomic DNA is crosslinked to nucleosomes and sequestered to the interphase. Accordingly, s_sonicated_chromatin is authored as a mixture containing retained crosslinked complexes, not as uniformly deproteinized DNA or evidence that sonication reverses crosslinks.

corrections.diagram_observation: The caption groups FAIRE-Seq and Sono-Seq above one fixation/sonication/aqueous-phase extraction route, without a method-specific branch or a size-selection label.
corrections.primary_statement: The Sono-Seq primary abstract explicitly combines sonication of crosslinked chromatin with size selection and massively parallel short-read sequencing and states that its breakage pattern is distinct from FAIRE. The candidate therefore adds only that supported abstract-level alternative block and does not treat the two method names as aliases or assign FAIRE partition selectivity to Sono-Seq. Exact Sono-Seq extraction/reversal order remains unresolved from the supplied evidence.

unknowns.question: For Sono-Seq specifically, which DNA fraction enters size selection, and does any phenol extraction precede or follow removal of protein-DNA crosslinks? The supplied primary evidence is abstract-only and does not establish these interfaces.
